summary: The new-chat screen's "Pick up where you left off" list leaves out an open hub child chat, as the desktop sidebar Recents already did. A child is started by its parent and is reached through it, so it takes no row of its own in a flat list. Both lists now read the same rule from src/shared/hub.ts (isHubChild), rather than each holding its own copy of the check.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No contract change. The rule itself lives in src/shared/hub.ts, which both lists read, but the backend keeps sending every chat with its `hub` field, as it already did for the sidebar; which rows a flat list draws is the client's choice. No channel, wire field or capability is added.

storageDataMigration.reason: Presentation only. The `hub` field of a list row is derived at read time from the open children the backend knows about; no table, column or stored format is read or written differently.

updateRelease.reason: No packaging, channel or compatibility change. An older backend that sends no `hub` field lists exactly what it did before.

automated: npm run typecheck passed for the main and renderer projects.

npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 passed. tests/unit/chat-landing.test.ts gains a case with a parent and two children in one project, where only the parent takes a row. The case was checked against the code with the filter removed, and it fails there.
notExercised: The phones were not changed. Both Home recents lists draw a child chat as its own row when `hub_children` is on, which is off by default on both; the named follow-up releases carry the same rule to them.
No screenshot baseline covers this list with a child chat: the visual fixture seeds hub children in a launch of its own, which opens on a chat and never on the new-chat screen.
